### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /profile — 1cr

Returns public profile information for a TikTok user — follower count, following count, total likes, bio, avatar URL, and verification status. `author.followers` is the unrounded integer when the source exposes it. When only the public rounded figure is available, the same integer field is returned and `author.ext.followers_approximate` is true. Pass either `handle` or `user_id`. Profiles with TikTok 'audience controls' enabled (a login/age wall in the browser) are supported when looked up by `handle`; for those gated accounts the following count and post count are not available and return null.

**Parameters**

- `handle` / `user_id` — at least one required.
  - `handle`: TikTok username without the @ symbol. (one of: handle, user_id — at least one required)
  - `user_id`: TikTok numeric user ID. Use this for faster responses. (one of: handle, user_id — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/videos — 1cr

Returns a paginated list of recent public videos posted by a TikTok user. Each video includes view count, like count, comment count, share count, caption, and thumbnail URL. Profiles with TikTok 'audience controls' enabled (a login/age wall in the browser) are supported when looked up by `handle`; page-1 order on those gated accounts may follow recency rather than pinned-first.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: TikTok username without the @ symbol
- `user_id` *(optional)*: TikTok user id. Use this for faster responses.
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: What to sort by
- `max_cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to get more videos. Get 'max_cursor' from previous response. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `region` *(optional)*: Region (Country) you want the proxy in. Defaults to US.
- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true for a trimmed down version of the response
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `max_cursor` (cursor style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile/videos?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post — 1cr

Returns detailed information about a specific TikTok video including view count, like count, comment count, share count, caption, music info, author details, and video metadata. When the creator added on-screen text with TikTok's built-in text tool, the overlay text is returned in `data.post.ext.on_screen_texts` (absent when the video has none — text burned in with an external editor is not detectable from post data).

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the TikTok video
- `region` *(optional)*: Region of the proxy. Sometimes you'll need to specify the region if you're not getting a response. Commonly for videos from the Phillipines, in which case you'd use 'PH'. Use 2 letter country codes like US, GB, FR, etc
- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true to get a trimmed response
- `download_media` *(optional)*: Set to true to also download the video/images and get back permanent, durable media URLs under `data.post.ext.download_media_urls` (`[{ post_id, cdn_url, type, cached }]`). Use these for archiving — the raw `media_urls` are short-lived signed CDN links that expire. Adds a few seconds of latency while the media is fetched.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/post?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post/comments — 1cr

Returns a list of comments on a specific TikTok video. Each comment includes the author username, comment text, like count, reply count, and creation timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the TikTok video to fetch comments for
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to get more comments. Get 'cursor' from previous response.
- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true to get a trimmed response

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/post/comments?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /video/comment/replies — 1cr

Fetches replies to a specific TikTok comment by its ID. Returns an array of comment objects each with text, user info, and creation time. Paginate with the cursor from the previous response.

**Parameters**

- `comment_id`: TikTok comment ID. This is the cid from the comments endpoint.
- `url`: TikTok video URL. This is the url from the comments endpoint.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to get more replies. Get 'cursor' from previous response.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/video/comment/replies?comment_id=<comment_id>&url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /comment — 2cr

Resolves a single TikTok comment to a live comment object (current like count, reply count, pinned flag, author, timestamp) without you paginating the comment section. Pass `comment_url` (a `.../@{handle}/video/{id}?comment_id={cid}` link, an `m.tiktok.com` share link, or a `vm.tiktok.com`/`.../t/` shortlink — resolved automatically) OR `post_url` + `comment_id`. For a reply, also pass `parent_comment_id` (a reply URL does not carry its parent). Instead of a comment id you can search the comment section: `author_username` (find a specific author's comments) or `text_contains` (exact snippet) return up to `max` matches. The response includes a `lookup.position_hint` — pass it back on a later lookup of the same comment to make the re-check nearly free. Flat 2 credits (6 with `deep_scan=true`, which widens the scan budget); a not-found returns 404 and is fully refunded.

**Parameters**

- `comment_url` *(optional)*: A TikTok comment URL: `https://www.tiktok.com/@{handle}/video/{videoId}?comment_id={cid}`, the `m.tiktok.com/v/{id}.html?...&share_comment_id={cid}` share form, or a `vm.tiktok.com/{code}` / `tiktok.com/t/{code}` shortlink. The `cid`/`comment_id`/`share_comment_id` query value may be numeric or the base64 form TikTok's share sheet emits (`?cid=NzY1...`) — both are accepted; base64 is decoded automatically. Mutually exclusive with `post_url`+`comment_id`.
- `post_url` *(optional)*: The post URL (`https://www.tiktok.com/@{handle}/video/{videoId}`). Combine with `comment_id`, or with `author_username`/`text_contains` for a search.
- `comment_id` *(optional)*: The target comment's numeric id (the `cid` from the comments endpoint). Requires `post_url`. Note that TikTok share links carry a base64-encoded `cid` — pass such a link as `comment_url` instead (decoded automatically), or base64-decode the value to its digits before passing it here.
- `parent_comment_id` *(optional)*: The parent comment's numeric id — supply this when the target is a reply so it can be resolved directly via the native replies endpoint.
- `author_username` *(optional)*: Return up to `max` comments authored by this username (no comment id needed). Mutually exclusive with `text_contains` and any comment id.
- `text_contains` *(optional)*: Return up to `max` comments whose text contains this snippet (case-insensitive). Mutually exclusive with `author_username` and any comment id.
- `deep_scan` *(optional)*: Widen the scan budget for deeply-buried comments (raises the page ceiling and deadline). Bills 6 credits instead of 2.
- `position_hint` *(optional)*: Opaque token from a prior lookup's `lookup.position_hint`. Passing it back probes the comment's last-known location first, making a re-check of an already-found comment cheap.
- `max` *(optional)*: For `author_username`/`text_contains` search: max matches to return (1–20, default 5).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/comment" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search — 1cr

Searches TikTok for videos matching a keyword query. Returns a list of matching videos with view counts, like counts, captions, author info, and thumbnails.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search keyword or phrase to find TikTok videos
- `date_posted` *(optional)*: Time Frame
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Sort by
- `region` *(optional)*: Note, this doesn't filter the tiktoks only in a specfic region, it puts the proxy there. Use it in case you want to scrape posts only available for some country. Use 2 letter country codes like US, GB, FR, etc
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to get more videos. Get 'cursor' from previous response.
- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true to get a trimmed response

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

Returns audience geography for a TikTok creator: audienceLocations ranks the top countries in the creator's audience with sampled follower counts and percentage share. Age and gender are not included — platforms do not expose those publicly.

Returns a list of followers for a TikTok user. Each follower includes username, display name, avatar, and follower count.

- `trim` *(optional)*: Set to true to get a trimmed response
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `min_time` (cursor style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `handle` / `user_id` — at least one required.
  - `handle`: TikTok username without the @ symbol (one of: handle, user_id — at least one required)
  - `user_id`: User id. Use this for faster response times. (one of: handle, user_id — at least one required)

```bash

  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /post/transcript — 10cr

Returns the transcript of a TikTok video. Supports auto-generated captions and AI-powered transcription as fallback.

> ⛔ **BANNED in this plugin: 10 credits, no advantage. Transcribe with the local captions→Groq→Whisper chain instead.**

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the TikTok video
- `language` *(optional)*: Language of the transcript. 2 letter language code, ie 'en', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'it', 'ja', 'ko', 'zh'
- `use_ai_as_fallback` *(optional)*: Set to 'true' to use AI as a fallback to get the transcript if the transcript is not found. Costs 10 credits to use this feature. And only if the video is under 2 minutes.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/post/transcript?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /video/screen-text — 5cr

Extracts the text shown ON the video itself — the overlay captions creators put on screen, which the regular caption and transcript never carry. Two layers are merged: native text-sticker data (present when the creator used TikTok's built-in text tool) and AI OCR of the video's cover frame, which also catches text burned in with editors like CapCut that no data provider returns. `texts` is the deduplicated union in reading order; `native_texts` and `ocr_texts` expose each layer separately and `source` says which layers produced data. A video with no on-screen text returns an empty `texts` array (that is a real answer, not an error). Costs 5 credits; auto-refunds when the video lookup or the whole extraction fails.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the TikTok video

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/video/screen-text?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/region — 1cr

Returns the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code for a public TikTok profile (e.g. `US` for United States, `MX` for Mexico). Useful for routing region-locked workflows and deduplicating profiles by country.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: TikTok username without the @ symbol

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile/region?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/full — 5cr

Fans out to the TikTok profile and recent-posts endpoints in parallel and returns the unified author, the recent-post list, and computed metrics — average engagement rate, posting cadence (with the window it was measured over), the top post, and the format mix. The profile leg is the only critical leg: if posts can't be fetched the call still returns the profile with post-dependent metrics null, and every leg's status is surfaced in legs[]. Flat 5 credits.

**Parameters**

- `handle` *(optional)*: handle
- `user_id` *(optional)*: user_id
- `posts` *(optional)*: How many recent posts to fetch + average the computed metrics over (1–100, default 25).
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Pass a prior response's posts_cursor to deepen the post window.
- `include` *(optional)*: CSV subset of posts,computed (default both). include=computed drops the raw posts[] to save payload.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/profile/full" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a TikTok endpoint

Almost everything here is 1 credit, which makes TikTok the cheapest deep-research platform in
the API. Only six endpoints cost more.

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Profile / their videos / one post | `/profile` · `/profile/videos` · `/post` | 1 |
| Search by keyword, hashtag, or top results | `/search` · `/search/hashtag` · `/search/top` | 1 |
| Find creators | `/search/users` | 1 |
| Comments, and replies to a comment | `/post/comments` · `/video/comment/replies` | 1 |
| Look up one comment by URL or id | `/comment` | 2 |
| Followers / following | `/user/followers` · `/user/following` | 1 |
| What audio is this, and who else used it | `/song` · `/song/videos` | 1 |
| Where is this creator based | `/profile/region` | 1 |
| Are they live right now | `/user/live` | 1 |
| **Audience demographics** | `/user/audience` | 5 |
| On-screen text burned into a video | `/video/screen-text` | 5 |
| The trending feed | `/trending` | 5 |
| Profile + posts + analytics in one call | `/profile/full` | 5 |
| ~~Transcript~~ | ⛔ `/post/transcript` is **banned** — use the local Whisper chain | — |

### The two endpoints worth paying 5cr for

**`/user/audience` (5cr)** is the only demographic read in the platform — who actually watches
a creator, rather than how many. For partnership or positioning questions that is the whole
answer, and there is no 1cr substitute.

**`/video/screen-text` (5cr)** extracts the text burned into the video frames. On short-form,
the on-screen hook usually *is* the hook — it is not in the caption. When you are studying why
a video worked, this reads the part that did the work.

### Format research runs on the 1cr endpoints

`/profile/videos` (1cr) returns views, likes and comments per item. Because independent
operators repeat what their private analytics tell them works, format repetition across
several creators is itself a performance signal — so a cheap sweep of several profiles beats
one expensive deep pull on a single account.

`/song/videos` (1cr) is the underrated one: it lists everyone using a given audio, which turns
a trending sound into a ready-made sample of creators competing on the same format.

## Field Maps


The `profile` endpoint returns an `Author` response normalized by the `tiktok-author` field map, and `post` returns a `Post` normalized by `tiktok-post`. Both include computed fields (`engagement_rate`, `language`, `content_category`, `estimated_reach`) under `data.computed`. Use `?format=raw` to bypass both and get the upstream JSON. Other TikTok endpoints are passthrough.
